title: A Droplet-Based Microfluidic Approach and Microsphere-PCR Amplification for Single-Stranded DNA Amplicons
protocol: Prepare 20 mL of liquid PDMS prepolymer by mixing base polymer and catalyst in a volume ratio of 10:1.
Pour 10 mL of the liquid PDMS onto a prepared SU-8 mold on a silicon wafer for the upper part of the microfluidic network.
Pour 10 mL of liquid PDMS on the silicon wafer without a mold structure for the bottom flat part.
Place two silicon wafers coated with liquid PDMS prepolymer on the hot plate and cure at 75 °C for 30 min.
Manually peel off the cured PDMS layer from the SU-8 mold.
Align a 1.5 mm diameter round hole punching tool to the oil port on the replicated microfluidic network.
Punch out the through-hole manually.
Repeat the punching process three times for the formation of the two solutions and the outlet port.
Perform hydrophilic surface treatment on both the upper and bottom PDMS layers using a hand-held corona treater.
Stack two plasma-treated PDMS layers and heat at 90 °C for 30 minutes using a hot plate for the PDMS-to-PDMS bonding process.
Supply pressurized water using a syringe pump into three inlet ports for structural bonding and leakage testing of the fabricated device.
Vortex and briefly centrifuge standard ssDNA acrydite labeled probe (Ap, 100 μM) and acrylamide:bis (19:1) stock solution.
Prepare solution I by mixing 25 μL of 40% acrylamide bis solution, 10 μL of ssDNA (acrydite probe), 10 μL of 5x TBE buffer, and 5 μL of water.
Prepare solution II with 50 μL of 20% ammonium persulfate.
Fill two syringes individually with solution I and solution II, and mount them onto the pump to introduce solution flows into the microfluidic platform.
Mix mineral oil with 0.4% TEMED for surface solidification of the microsphere.
Fill a glass bottle with 4 mL of the mineral oil to generate a continuous flow.
Insert two tubes to the pneumatic port and fluid port in the cap of the glass bottle.
Connect tubes between the glass bottle and the oil port in the microfluidic device.
Connect tubes to the two solution ports in the microfluidic device from the syringe pumps.
Insert tubes to the outlet port to transfer generated microspheres into a beaker.
Set the flow rate of the syringe pump to 0.4 - 0.7 mL/h.
Adjust compressed air pressure using a regulator to 82 - 116 kPa.
Set the rotational speed of the magnetic stirrer bar in the glass beaker on a hot plate to 500 rpm.
Operate the syringe pump and supply compressed air into the glass bottle using an electromagnetic valve's ON/OFF control.
Observe formation of microspheres in the flow-focusing geometry with a digital microscope.
Monitor solidification of generated microspheres in the glass beaker.
Take approximately 100 μL of aqueous solution of polyacrylamide oligo-microspheres and place on the glass hemocytometer.
Gently fill the microsphere suspension up to the well of the counting chamber.
Count microspheres in one set of 16 squares using a microscope and hand tally counter.
Move the hemocytometer to the next set of the chamber and continue counting until all four sets of 16 corners are counted.
Determine the average microsphere count.
Calculate the number of microspheres in the original bead suspension.
Transfer 100 μL of microspheres to a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Remove the supernatant through gentle centrifuging at 400 x g.
Pipette out the remaining solution gently.
Resuspend Cy3-cAp using 100 μL of 1xTE buffer in order to achieve a final concentration of 100 μM.
Add 100 μM of Cy3-cAp to a sterile 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube containing Ap-copolymerized microspheres.
Tap the tube a few times to mix and incubate at room temperature in the dark for 1 h.
Discard the supernatant and remove residual buffer through pipetting.
Rinse three times with 500 μL of TE buffer.
Resuspend microspheres by gently tapping the microcentrifuge tube.
Place microspheres on the glass slide (75 mm x 50 mm) and cover with aluminum foil prior to imaging.
Thaw reagents in Table 4 on ice, except Taq polymerase enzyme which should be stored at -20°C until needed.
Gently vortex all reagents and then briefly centrifuge tubes at 10,000 x g for 10 s.
Combine all reagents as described in Table 4.
Place samples into a thermocycler and start the asymmetric PCR under the following conditions: 25 cycles (95 °C for 30 s, 52 °C for 30 s, and 72 °C for 30 s), 85 °C for 5 min, hold at 4 °C.
Prepare microsphere-PCR reagent mix.
Thaw the reagents on ice, except Taq polymerase enzyme which should be stored at -20°C.
Gently vortex all thawed reagents and briefly centrifuge tubes at 10,000 x g for 10 seconds.
Count approximately 25 microspheres through microscopic counting using a light microscope with 40X magnification.
Combine all reagents as described in Table 6.
Place samples into a thermocycler and start the asymmetric PCR program.
Run the PCR program under the following conditions:
Cycle at 95 °C for 30 seconds, then cycle at 52 °C for 30 seconds, followed by cycling at 72 °C for 30 seconds (repeat for 25 cycles).
Hold at 85 °C for 5 minutes.
Hold samples at 4 °C.
Add 8 μL of 6x loading buffer to each amplified sample.
Load 15 μL of each sample into a 2% agarose gel.
Perform electrophoresis at 100 V for 35 min in 1x TAE buffer.
Fix hybridized microspheres to the stage of the microscope in a holder.
Select the laser (Helium/Neon, 543 nm) and turn it on in laser control.
Select the objective lens in microscope control.
Select the desired filter for Cy3 and channel in configuration control.
Start the experiment and observe the sample.
